question: Is LOBSTR legit, and where does my recovery phrase live?

golden.answer: LOBSTR is a real, currently maintained third-party wallet operated under the Ultra Stellar identity, with a current official Apple app listing as of 2026-08-31; that establishes the provider/publisher, not risk-free safety or SDF endorsement. Current LOBSTR documentation says keys for current or migrated accounts are encrypted with user-password participation and stored locally/on-device, while accounts created before 2020-09-01 that were never migrated are a documented exception. Its 12-word Recovery Phrase (or older wallet-specific 10-word Recovery Code) must be kept private/offline; LOBSTR says it cannot reconstruct users’ phrase, code, secret, or password. Install only from links reached through `lobstr.co`, verify the app publisher, and use 2FA plus multisig or hardware signing when the threat model warrants it.
keyFacts: Identifies LOBSTR as an active Ultra Stellar third-party wallet.
Dates the LOBSTR activity assessment to an observation date.
Attributes local/on-device storage to current LOBSTR documentation.
Requires credentials to remain unshared and support-unrecoverable per current LOBSTR docs.
avoid: Do NOT say a wallet provider or SDF can recover a secret phrase you lost.
Do NOT claim the LOBSTR brand name makes any download link or support contact safe.
Do NOT say app-store presence or popularity proves cryptographic safety.
Do NOT make an era-independent claim that every LOBSTR key was always stored only locally or only server-side.
golden.notes: Status phrased to avoid turning a dated product assessment into a permanent guarantee.

corroboration.claim: Current LOBSTR documentation says current or migrated keys are generated and decrypted on-device with password participation, and that an encrypted copy of the Recovery phrase/Secret key is also stored on LOBSTR servers.

evidence.note: 'The keys themselves can only be decrypted and accessed by users on-device'; 'We store the encrypted version of the Recovery phrase/Secret key on our server'; 'The transaction signing also happens locally on-device'. Owner documentation only; no class F audit, so the storage claim stays source-relative and the avoid item forbids an era-independent local-only or server-only claim.

Migration overview: pre-September 1, 2020 wallets kept keys on the platform in encrypted form; stated migration deadline July 10, 2026 has passed, and the documented exception remains for unmigrated wallets.

corroboration.claim: Current LOBSTR documentation requires credentials to stay unshared and states that support cannot reconstruct a lost Recovery phrase, code, secret, or password.

evidence.note: 'Do not share your Recovery Phrase and Secret key with anyone'; 'We (the LOBSTR team) do not have access to users' Recovery phrases, Secret keys, Recovery codes, or Account passwords.'

The recovery tool requires the user's Recovery code or Recovery Phrase plus the account email; staff approval is a process gate, not reconstruction. The restore article's 'Only share your Recovery Phrase with trusted services' is ordinary English for services the user elects to trust (blind lane: no product or docs-index hit for a named 'trusted services' product), so it does not contradict the unshared-credential rule.
Independent sweep (lane A D6) found an active publisher and current app; user allegations found in the sweep did not establish provider fraud or cryptographic safety.
